Senses.Explanation: To hesitate and deliberate is to hang back weighing a response instead of answering directly. Chan exchanges repeatedly pair that delay with already missing, immediate distance, a blow or shout, or a prohibition on deliberation. The corpus pairs it with an immediate cut-off. As a verdict clause: "deliberate and you're already off," (擬議即乖 6), "…and you already miss," (擬議即差 7), set beside the parallel "open your mouth and it's already remote" (開口即邈) in (開口即邈)，(擬議即差). As the trigger of a blow or shout: "wait for him to deliberate, then hit," (待伊擬議便打 擬議便打 18), (僧擬議師便喝). As a barred delay: "permits no deliberating," (不容擬議 116), "cannot deliberate one's way to it," (擬議不來 97). And figured as a spatial gulf: (擬議之間)，(白雲萬里) / "in the space of deliberating, ten-thousand miles of white cloud / a long road," (長途萬里 擬議之間 91), "the moment you hesitate and deliberate, blood has already spattered the Brahma-heaven" (你纔擬議，早是血濺梵天了也). Collocation (擬議思量) (135). The texts state the cut-off and the gulf as facts of deployment and add no further gloss, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide term. Curated occurrences are stock formula-deployments (verdict clauses, blow/shout triggers, gulf images) by unnamed masters, so MasterName is null. Attested pairings: (開口即邈) (companion), (便打) / (便喝) (consequence), (白雲萬里) / (長途萬里) / (血濺梵天) (gulf images). Counts: (擬議) 4329/359; (擬議之間) 91; (不容擬議) 116; (擬議不來) 97; (擬議思量) 135.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直下便見，無第二人，擬議即乖，焉容鈍置？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xueguan (雪關禪師語錄), repentance-hall informal address. Xueguan Zhiyin is the exact speaker: describing original-ground scenery, he says it is seen directly with no second person and that deliberation immediately goes astray.

Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Shimen Yuncong's recorded sayings. Shimen Yuncong is the exact speaker: the level-one section names Chan Master Cizhao Yuncong, and his uninterrupted hall address closes, 'open your mouth and it is already distant; deliberate and it is already wrong.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 如金剛王寶劍，你纔擬議，早是血濺梵天了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Collected Chan Comments on Old Cases (宗門拈古彙集) explicitly introduces Luohan Ji's comment. Luohan Ji is the exact speaker: after contrasting two readings of Manjusri's answer, he says that as soon as you begin to deliberate, blood is already splashed across Brahma's heaven.

The Recorded Sayings of the Monk Tianyin (天隱和尚語錄), New Year's Day hall address. Tianyin Yuanxiu is the exact speaker: after dancing with the staff he introduces and quotes the saying that amid deliberation white clouds are ten thousand miles away.
The Jiatai Universal Lamp Record (嘉泰普燈錄), Furong Daokai section. Complete-case exact-turn review identifies Furong Daokai as the exact speaker of this occurrence.

Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Yunmen Wenyan's Essential Sayings from the Master's Room. Yunmen Wenyan is the exact speaker: in his own instruction he says to wait until the other person deliberates and then strike.

Occurrences.Kwic: 三世諸佛不知有狸奴白牯卻知有僧擬議師便喝落堂
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of National Teacher Yulin Pushing Universal Relief (普濟玉琳國師語錄), public instruction. The exact actor is the unnamed deliberating monk: the grammar says 'there was a monk who deliberated' (有僧擬議), followed by Yulin Tongxiu shouting and leaving the hall; the complete case and all six ladder rungs give the monk no personal name.

Occurrences.Kwic: 喚作竹篦則觸，不喚作竹篦則背。速道，速道！擬議不來，劈脊便棒。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi (楚石梵琦禪師語錄). Complete-case exact-turn review identifies Chushi Fanqi as the exact speaker of this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 射透鐵圍不容擬議。一言之下殺活全彰。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), in Yuanwu Keqin's own hall address. Yuanwu Keqin says that shooting through the iron enclosure permits no deliberation and that killing and giving life are fully disclosed under one word.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州狗子無佛性狗無佛性，全提正令，擬議思量，錯過窮命。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Miyun (密雲禪師語錄), in Miyun Yuanwu's own verse on Zhaozhou's dog. Miyun Yuanwu joins deliberation and thinking to missing it for one's whole life.
